item.research_question: How can a dual-oxide shell of ZnO/Al2O3 be designed via atomic layer deposition to simultaneously achieve record-high microwave absorption in low-frequency bands and enhanced anti-corrosion properties for FeSiAl alloys?
item.material_system: FeSiAl (FSA) core with ZnO and Al2O3 dual-oxide shells (FSA@ZnO@Al2O3), compared to single-shell variants (FSA@ZnO, FSA@Al2O3) and annealed FSA (FSA-500)
item.processing_route: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) at 150 °C using N2 carrier gas; ZnO deposited via diethyl zinc (DEZn) and H2O (250 cycles, 0.02 s dose, 8 s purge); Al2O3 deposited via trimethylaluminum (TMA) under identical conditions; followed by annealing at 500 °C under N2 for 2 h
item.test_conditions: Microwave absorption measured in 0.5–18 GHz frequency range with thicknesses 0.5–5.0 mm; corrosion tests conducted in 5.0 wt% NaCl solution using a three-electrode system (OCP ~1600 s, Tafel scan -500 to 500 mV vs OCP at 1 mV s−1, EIS 10^5 to 10^-2 Hz with 5 mV perturbation)
key_findings: FSA@ZnO@Al2O3 achieved a minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of -50.6 dB at 3.4 GHz, compared to -13.5 dB for pure FSA.
The effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of FSA@ZnO@Al2O3 increased up to ~3 times that of pure FSA (1.5 GHz vs 0.5 GHz at ~4.0 GHz).
The anti-corrosion property of the FSA core was improved by 9.0 times compared to bare FSA in 5.0 wt% NaCl solution.
The corrosion rate of FSA@ZnO@Al2O3 decreased by about 9.0 times relative to pristine FSA.
The charge transfer resistance (Rct) and impedance modulus |Z|0.01 Hz of FSA@ZnO@Al2O3 were the highest among all samples.
The corrosion potential (Ecorr) shifted positively to 0.0191 V for FSA@ZnO@Al2O3, compared to -0.1783 V for pure FSA.
The anodic current density of FSA@ZnO@Al2O3 was at least 1.0 order of magnitude lower than that of pure FSA.
item.mechanism: Microwave absorption is enhanced by dielectric loss from ZnO/Al2O3 shells (interfacial polarization, Debye relaxation), magnetic loss from the DO3 superlattice structure of the FSA core, improved impedance matching in L/S bands, and high attenuation characteristics. Anti-corrosion is achieved via multistage barriers that obstruct corrosive media (Cl-, H2O, O2) and increase charge transfer resistance, effectively blocking the electric circuit.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The authors propose the FSA@ZnO@Al2O3 gradient structure as a promising platform for the design of next-generation microwave absorbers with improved anti-corrosion properties.
quotes: The corrosion resistance is improved by the unique multistage oxide barriers.
The RLmin value and effective bandwidth of this designed novel absorber increased up to ~ 3.7 and ~ 3 times, respectively.
